references.text: Previous instructions on building an altar for the Lord, which form the basis for the detailed specifications in this verse.
Describes the actual construction of the bronze altar with the same dimensions: five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
Use of acacia wood (שִׁטִּים) for holy objects, the same material used for the ark of the covenant.
The incense altar, also made of acacia wood, but with different dimensions - showing the contrast between the two altars in the tabernacle.
Solomon's temple had a much larger bronze altar, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple includes an altar with detailed measurements, pointing back to the tabernacle altar.
The book of Hebrews refers to our having an altar from which those who serve in the tabernacle have no right to eat - a typological fulfillment in Christ.
John sees in his vision the altar in heaven, which is the heavenly pattern for the earthly altar in the tabernacle.
Confirms that the actual construction of the bronze altar followed exactly the specific measurements given in the instructions.
